core_meaning.primary_meaning: Sabih corresponds to the Arabic form صَبِيح and is glossed in this record as “Beautiful, handsome.” The record associates the form with root ص ب ح (ṣ-b-ḥ). The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Sabih corresponds to the Arabic form صَبِيح (Arabic root ص ب ح (ṣ-b-ḥ); صَبِيح (Ṣabīḥ)). Its core sense is sabih; beautiful, handsome. Sabih is Arabic صَبِيح (Ṣabīḥ) 'beautiful, handsome', from the root ص ب ح (ṣ-b-ḥ). CRITICAL SOURCE ERROR: the source gave سبح (a different form). The source gloss 'Patient, Steadfast' is unsupported and has been replaced with the lexical sense. CRITICAL SOURCE ERROR: the source labelled the gender unisex; documented usage is predominantly male.
